The Supreme Court on Wednesday (October 28) has upheld the grant of a War Injury pension to ex-armed forces personnel for the ailment which developed owing to his posting at Kargil as part of Operation Rakshak.

A bench of Justice Pamidighantam Sri Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe dismissed the Union government's appeal against the High Court's and Armed Forces Tribunal's order which granted a War Injury pension to the ex-personnel in place of the disability pension.

At the same time, the Court also suggested that the government issue a comprehensive and clearly identifiable subordinate legislation governing the services of ex-personnel who became eligible for a War Injury Pension, noting that there is uncertainty about which Rules, Regulations, Instructions and Policies of the Ministry of Defence (MoD) are applicable.
“We continue to wonder why this uncertainty about applicable rules continues.
It is high time that the MoD issues a comprehensive and clearly identifiable subordinate legislation governing the services.
This is necessary for fairness in action and also for good governance.”, the Court said.
The respondent Narender Kumar joined the Indian Army in December 1996 and was posted at Kargil from July 2003 to July 2005.
During this posting, he was diagnosed with seropositive rheumatoid arthritis in January 2005.
He was subsequently diagnosed with two spinal conditions while posted in West Bengal.
When he was discharged from service in January 2013, the Release Medical Board assessed his disabilities as aggravated by military service at 70%, rounded off to 75% for life.
He was granted disability pension comprising service and disability elements.

article_sentences: All major rivers, rivulets, seasonal streams across Srikakulam, Parvatipuram-Manyam and Vizianagaram districts were in spate after their catchment areas received huge inflow of waters under the impact of the very severe cyclonic storm Arnab that crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast near Yanam, in the early hours of Wednesday.

According to data provided by the Srikakulam district administration, the average rainfall in normal conditions is only 136.5 mm but the district received 4,094.2 mm rainfall between 8 a.m. on Tuesday and 8 a.m. on Wednesday.
Heavy rainfall in the district and upstream catchment areas led to increased inflows into the rivers Vamsadhara, Nagavali, Mahindra Tanaya, Bahuda and others.
The Narayanpur Anicut on the Nagavali river received 38,100 cusecs of water.
The Irrigation Department released a similar quantity downstream.
The old bridge over the Nagavali river in Srikakulam town was in spate with the release of water into the Narayanpur Anicut.
The Gotta barrage on the Vamsadhara river received 6,544 cusecs of water in the early hours of Wednesday.
Srikakulam District Collector Swapnil Dinakar Pundkar who visited Polaki and other mandals told.
The Hindu that the situation was under control with the precautionary steps taken up by the government.
He said that irrigation, revenue, Roads and Buildings departments were alerted to take necessary steps in flood affected areas.

Rivers such as Suvarnamukhi, Vegavati and others are receiving huge inflows of water but there is no immediate threat of floods for Parvatipuram, Seethanagaram, Bobbili and other areas, according to officials.

stories.headline: Israelis await final election results as Netanyahu rivals weigh joining forces with Arab parties
stories.title: Israelis await final election results as Netanyahu rivals weigh joining forces with Arab parties
stories.summary: Jerusalem, Oct 28: Anxious Israelis watched election results near completion Wednesday after the highest voter turnout in over a quarter-century, as no clear winner emerged and weeks of negotiating could lie ahead for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and an array of opposition parties trying to unseat him. Arab-led parties made a historic showing, but it's not clear if other opponents of Netanyahu's far-right government would form a coalition with them for a majority of seats in parliament. Issues around the Palestinians and their descendants remain incredibly sensitive in Israel. Netanyahu seeks to remain the country's longest-serving prime minister. In defiant comments after the vote, he dismissed the idea of partnering with Arab parties — whose constituents make up 20 per cent of Israel's population — as treasonous. On Wednesday, Netanyahu warned against a “dangerous government” that might include them. He won't work with the Arab-led parties, and they have ruled that out, too. His top challenger, centrist former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, has left the door open to partnering with Arab parties under certain conditions, including their recognition of Israel as a Jewish state and of Hamas as an extremist group. But it's not clear whether some of Eisenkot's likely partners who have ruled out such an alliance will change their minds to force Netanyahu from office. Israeli voters choose parties, not individuals. With 85 per cent of votes counted, Netanyahu's Likud party has 20.8 per cent and Eisenkot's Yashar party has 16.1 per cent. The official count does not indicate how many seats each will have in parliament, the 120-seat Knesset. Emerging results indicated that neither Netanyahu's nor Eisenkot's coalition blocs would reach the 61 seats needed for a majority. Likud's vote share declined from 23.4 per cent in the previous election in 2022. Netanyahu faces a setback but not outright defeat Nearly 78 per cent of eligible voters turned out, the highest since 1999. Final results are expected in the coming days, including from hundreds of thousands of absentee ballots yet to be counted from military personnel and diplomats. Voting reflected unease over Netanyahu's alliance with the far-right and anger in a war-weary nation over military draft exemptions for the significant ultra-Orthodox Jewish population. But results suggest opponents were unable to capitalise on the grief caused by the Hamas-led October 7, 2023, attack to decisively push him from office. One partner losing support, however, was far-right national security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir. For many Israelis, he represented the worst strain of Netanyahu's government, openly taunting Palestinian detainees and asserting that many in Gaza are “not even people.” Vote-counting suggested Likud would remain the largest party and best placed to be tapped to form a government by Israel's president, Isaac Herzog. The president, however, isn't required to task the leader of the party holding the most seats. “We must do everything we can, certainly after yesterday, to avoid another round of elections,” Herzog said Wednesday. The most obvious path to a parliamentary majority could involve Eisenkot partnering with Arab-led parties — which have 14.9 per cent of the votes counted — but that's politically challenging. In a speech early Wednesday that focused on national unity, Eisenkot pledged to form a government and promised “a new era — an era of hope." If no one can put together a majority coalition, new elections could be held early next year. Israel held five elections between April 2019 and November 2022 because of a similar stalemate. Whether thousands of Israelis living abroad would again fly back home to vote, and whether Arab voters would again surge to the polls, is unclear. Minority governments also are possible, but they must rely on cooperation from parties outside the government to pass legislation. Arab-led parties could hold the key Confronted with Arab parties' strong election showing, Israelis have renewed a debate about identity. “We have no future here if we do not stop being afraid," said Yair Golan, whose Democrats party supports bringing Arab-led parties into a coalition. "We must no longer accept Netanyahu's racist division between Jewish votes and Arab votes.” Israel's Arab citizens are descendants of Palestinians who remained in the state after its creation in 1948. They often face discrimination and are viewed with wariness because of their solidarity with the Palestinian cause. That suspicion intensified after October 7, even though Arab citizens were also among those killed and abducted. The mood was joyful overnight at the headquarters of the United Arab List, the lone Arab party to ever join a governing coalition, briefly, in 2021. “We are here, we are not on the sidelines,” party leader Mansour Abbas declared. Some Israelis found that an unusual, if not uncomfortable, prospect. “We are little by little coming to a situation where we have to face reality," said Hanna Doukhan, a voter in Tel Aviv. "I don't see a possibility to form a government without the Arabs.” Others were hopeful. “This would open the door to repairing our society" while preserving Israel as the national home of the Jewish people, said Eti Wissotzky-Cohen in Tel Aviv. And in Nazareth, one of Israel's largest Arab cities, Awni Zoabi thanked God for a possible return to rationality in a country where extreme rhetoric has increased. “The Arabic language has become as if it were a crime," Zoabi said. Attitudes over Netanyahu will shape the days ahead Netanyahu has had a nearly unbroken 17-year rule. Israelis were divided over him even before the deadliest attack in the country's history. The resulting wars, along with settler violence in the occupied West Bank, have stoked worldwide outrage, straining ties with Israel's closest allies and fueling a rise in antisemitism. Netanyahu's supporters believe he is protecting Israel's security and Jewish identity in the face of international pressure and liberal elites at home. “I prefer that (Netanyahu) assembles the coalition,” said Ran Cohen, a Jerusalem resident. “He's the only one who knows how to do the job properly, knows how to speak to the world.” Detractors say Netanyahu, facing an ongoing corruption trial, dragged out the war in Gaza and its hostage crisis for political reasons. They say he is undermining Israel's independent judiciary. And they accuse his government of allowing ultra-Orthodox religious Jews to avoid military conscription. Eisenkot is viewed by supporters as a capable leader with sterling security credentials. His son and two nephews were killed in Gaza, and his backers believe that he feels deeply the country's pain. Parties that likely would partner with him have vowed to improve Israel's international standing and work to conscript ultra-Orthodox men while bolstering the independence of the judiciary.

article_sentences: Leader of Opposition in the Assembly R. Ashok has accused the State Election Commission (SEC) of violating norms to facilitate irregularities in the proposed GBA polls by printing 90 lakh voters’ identity cards in Bengaluru at a cost of ₹20 crore after the announcement of Special Intensive Revision (SIR) by the Election Commission of India.
Alleging that the Congress government was involved in these irregularities, Mr. Ashok demanded a CBI probe into the episode.
However, the SEC strongly denied these allegations by stating that the tenders had been floated before the announcement of SIR and that it had acted within its legal mandate.
Addressing a press conference in Bengaluru, Mr. Ashok alleged that the SEC had printed 90 lakh cards, though the total number of voters in Bengaluru had been pegged at around 59 lakh after the SIR.
Pointing out that the SEC was now left with an additional 31 lakh voters identity cards, he described these additional cards as “bogus” and alleged that they would be used for “vote theft”.
He alleged that the Congress government had got this done to commit irregularities in the proposed election to GBA.

“The State Election Commission did this though it had filed an affidavit in the Supreme Court stating that elections to local bodies would be held only after the SIR and after the new voters’ list is prepared,“ he said.
Denying the allegations, SEC Secretary Amaresh H. said the tender was called before the SIR was announced.
Mr. Amaresh said the tender was issued under Rule 26 of the Greater Bengaluru Governance (Registration of Electors) Rules, 2025, which provides for the printing of voter identity cards.

After Justice Bhanot entered the courtroom, the AGA raised the issue with him.
The association alleged that the judge pointed a finger at the lawyer, used harsh language and ordered that he be sent to jail.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Cancels Bail Of Man Accused Of Sharing Sensitive Military Information With Pakistan
stories.title: Supreme Court Cancels Bail Of Man Accused Of Sharing Sensitive Military Information With Pakistan
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday set aside a Rajasthan High Court order that had granted regular bail to an accused in an espionage case solely because the grounds of arrest were not furnished to him in writing.

“A hyper-technical objection regarding the form or mode of communicating grounds of arrest cannot be treated as a self-executing, blanket key to unlock regular bail, bypassing the core parameters governing bail jurisprudence,” the bench held.

A bench of Justice MM Sundresh and Justice Prasanna B Varale made the observations while directing the respondent Jhabra Ram to surrender within two weeks from the date of the order, while reiterating that communication of grounds of arrest is a crucial constitutional and statutory safeguard, but held that the record showed substantial and effective compliance in the case, and that no prejudice had been found.

The case deals with offences under Sections 3 and 9 of the Official Secrets Act, 1923 (OSA), and Sections 152 and 238(b) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS), alleging that the respondent was in contact with foreign handlers belonging to a Pakistani intelligence agency and was transmitting sensitive military photographs, videos and troop movement details from Pokhran and Jaisalmer in exchange for financial benefits.
The respondent was served several notices calling him to appear before interrogation centres, before the FIR was registered.
Subsequently, an FIR was registered against him which led to his arrest on 30 January 2026.
The Arrest Memo was read over to him in the presence of two witnesses and bears his signature.
At the same time, his brother was also informed telephonically of his arrest, as recorded in an Arrest Information Memo.

On 31 January 2026, the respondent was produced before the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate where he opposed police custody remand on merits, but neither he nor his counsel raised any grievance about non-communication of grounds of arrest.

His regular bail plea was rejected by the Additional District and Sessions Judge on 10 March 2026, which held that the signed Arrest Memo amounted to compliance in substance with Section 47 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS).
Later, on 18 May 2026, the High Court granted bail on the basis that the grounds of arrest were not furnished in writing before or at the time of remand.
It held that oral intimation or case diary entries did not satisfy Section 47 BNSS in light of Mihir Rajesh Shah v State of Maharashtra.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court has stayed a Punjab and Haryana High Court order restraining judicial officers in Rohtak Sessions Division from entertaining bail applications in a case involving an alleged large-scale real estate investment scam in which investors were allegedly cheated of crores of rupees.
A bench of Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice K Vinod Chandran passed the order on October 27 while hearing a special leave petition filed challenging the High Court's September 30 order.
The Court issued notice, returnable in four weeks, and stayed the operation of the impugned order in the meantime.
“Issue notice, returnable in four weeks.
Dasti service, in addition, is permitted.
In the meantime, there shall be stay of operation of the impugned order dated 30.09.2026 passed by the High Court of Punjab & Haryana at Chandigarh in CRM M-42815/2026”, the Court ordered.

The High Court had passed the order while hearing an anticipatory bail petition filed by Subhash Gupta, a partner of Gupta Property Developers, Shivji, in connection with an FIR under Sections 420, 120-B and 506 of the IPC, corresponding to Sections 318(4), 61 and 351(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

In its order, the High Court had expressed serious concern over the investigation, observing that attempts had been made to shield the main accused, who are accused of cheating numerous investors of crores of rupees by collecting money for real estate projects without delivering possession or returning the invested amounts.
The High Court had noted that, despite earlier directions, the investigation had not proceeded properly.

It noted that a Special Investigation Team headed by Rohtak Superintendent of Police Gaurav Rajpurohit was investigating the case and that Kuldeep Kumar Tahlan, a director of DHL Infratech Private Limited, and Gurvinder Jeet Singh, an employee of Gupta Property Developers, had been arrested.
The Court noted that Kuldeep Kumar Tahlan had been granted bail, whereas Gurvinder Jeet Singh's bail plea had been dismissed by the courts at Rohtak.

It further observed that three directors of DHL Infratech and its authorised signatory, Sidhant, had been granted interim anticipatory bail by the same presiding officer who had dismissed the bail plea of the petitioner before the High Court.

article_sentences: The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved Pradhan Mantri Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana, a new scheme to enable panchayats identify their local resources and constraints, and prepare development plans based on their specific needs.
As part of capacity building under the scheme, the Centre will also train elected representatives as well as officials in the 3-tier panchayati raj system.

Briefing media after the Cabinet meeting, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw called it a paradigm shift from prescription-based schemes to a model focused on local-level capacity building and planning.
The scheme is approved for implementation from current fiscal till 2030-31, with an outlay of ₹7,395.55 crore — Central share of ₹4,869.48 crore and State share of ₹2,526.07 crore.

A major focus of the scheme is capacity-building of elected representatives as general and specialised training will be provided to elected representatives to improve their functioning and governance capabilities, he said.
The scheme seeks to financially empower panchayats through better utilisation of Finance Commission grants and mobilisation of own-source revenue, to make them more self-reliant, he added.

Sources said that though it is a new scheme, but it has also all the features of the previous Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA), including its many components like the e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project (MMP), which was not extended after it ended in FY26.
Under RGSA, the Centre had released to States ₹800.17 crore in 2023-24, ₹670.40 crore in 2024-25 and ₹730.75 crore in April-February of 2025-26.

The Pradhan Mantri Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana will be implemented through the respective State governments in which States and Union Territories will submit Annual Action Plans specifying activities, priorities and requirements in accordance with the scheme’s objectives and guidelines, an official statement said.
The designated Central Empowered Committee will appraise and approve these plans in accordance with applicable procedures and norms.
The Central Government and States will undertake activities within their respective areas of responsibility, supported by coordination, technical assistance, monitoring and review.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Asks Law Commission To Recommend Measures For Speedy Execution Of Arbitral Awards
stories.title: Supreme Court Asks Law Commission To Recommend Measures For Speedy Execution Of Arbitral Awards
stories.summary: A 24-year delay in the enforcement of an award forced the Court to make the intervention.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: A 24-year delay in the enforcement of an award forced the Court to make the intervention.

The Supreme Court on Wednesday (October 28) requested the Law Commission of India to undertake a focused study of the statutory and procedural framework governing the enforcement and execution of arbitral awards and recommend measures to ensure their timely enforcement.

A bench of Justices Vikram Nath, Sandeep Mehta and Aparesh Kumar Singh said that the prolonged execution of arbitral awards undermines the very objective of arbitration as an effective alternative to conventional civil litigation.
The Court observed that even after an award is rendered and survives judicial challenge, the successful party may be forced to undergo another prolonged round of litigation to realise its benefits.

“The promise of arbitration remains unfulfilled if a party, having traversed the arbitral process, is compelled to embark upon another protracted course of litigation to secure the benefit of the award,” the Court observed.
The judgment was passed in an appeal arising from a dispute in an international commercial arbitration between Iraq-based Royal Construction Company Pvt.
and National Projects Construction Corporation concerning the enforcement of an arbitral award rendered in 2002.
More than 24 years after the award, the parties were still litigating over its enforcement.
The Court noted that the efficacy of the arbitration regime cannot be assessed merely by the speed with which an award is rendered or the limited grounds available to challenge it.
It must also be assessed by whether the successful party can realise the fruits of the award within a reasonable time.

It observed that Section 36 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 provides for the enforcement of arbitral awards in the same manner as decrees of courts, thereby relying on the ordinary execution machinery under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

The Court identified several aspects warranting focused scrutiny, including the identification and disclosure of the award-debtor's assets, coordination between different modes of execution, disposal of repetitive or dilatory objections, and the time taken to conclude execution proceedings.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Upholds Bombay High Court Ruling Setting Aside ₹8,415 Crore YES Bank AT-1 Bond Write-Down
stories.title: Supreme Court Upholds Bombay High Court Ruling Setting Aside ₹8,415 Crore YES Bank AT-1 Bond Write-Down
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has dismissed appeals filed by YES Bank Limited, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Union of India, upholding the Bombay High Court's decision setting aside the permanent write-down of YES Bank's Additional Tier-1 (AT-1) bonds worth ₹8,415 crore.

A Bench of Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Augustine George Masih held that the Administrator of YES Bank could not write down the bonds in contravention of the final YES Bank Limited Reconstruction Scheme, 2020, particularly when the provision expressly providing for the write-down had been omitted from the notified scheme.
The dispute arose from the Administrator's decision dated March 14, 2020, to permanently write down the AT-1 bonds following the reconstruction of the bank.
The bonds had been issued in two tranches of ₹3,000 crore and ₹5,415 crore.

The Court observed that the omission of the write-down provision from the final Reconstruction Scheme, considered alongside the deliberative process preceding its notification, indicated that the Central Government had consciously decided not to incorporate such a provision.
The Administrator could not rely on a general savings clause in the scheme to claim specific authority to write down the bonds.
The Court also examined the RBI's Basel III Capital Regulations and the Information Memoranda governing the bonds.
It considered whether the conditions authorising a write-down had been satisfied and whether the Administrator had acted in accordance with the applicable regulatory and contractual framework.
Upholding the Bombay High Court's decision, the Supreme Court held that the Administrator's action was impermissible.
The appeals were accordingly dismissed.
The Court further clarified that the annual coupon payments would remain unaffected by the outcome of the appeals and must be made in accordance with the Information Memoranda.
Dua Associates represented ECL Finance Limited, Respondent No. 14, before the Supreme Court.

stories.headline: Cabinet approves 3% DA hike for 48.54 lakh central government employees, 68.71 lakh pensioners
stories.title: Cabinet approves 3% DA hike for 48.54 lakh central government employees, 68.71 lakh pensioners
stories.summary: New Delhi [India], October 28 : The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved a 3 per cent increase in Dearness Allowance (DA) for Central Government employees and Dearness Relief (DR) for pensioners, effective July 1, 2026, providing relief against rising prices. The move will raise DA and DR rates from the existing 60 per cent to 63 per cent of basic pay and pension, respectively. The increase is expected to benefit approximately 48.54 lakh Central Government employees and 68.71 lakh pensioners across the country. According to the government, the combined annual financial implication of the increase in DA and DR will be Rs 10,016.10 crore, adding to the Centre's expenditure. The additional instalment of DA and DR has been approved in accordance with the accepted formula based on the recommendations of the 7th Central Pay Commission. Dearness Allowance is paid to serving government employees to help offset the impact of inflation on their cost of living. Dearness Relief serves a similar purpose for pensioners, helping them manage the effect of rising prices on their pension income. The revision will be applicable retrospectively from July 1, 2026, meaning eligible employees and pensioners will be entitled to the revised rates from that date. The Cabinet's decision comes as the government continues to adjust inflation-linked benefits for its employees and pensioners through periodic revisions in DA and DR. The increase in these allowances is linked to an established formula and is intended to help protect the purchasing power of government employees and pensioners against price increases. With the latest revision, both serving employees and pensioners will receive an additional three percentage points over the previous rate of 60 per cent of basic pay or pension, respectively. The decision covers Central Government employees and pensioners and will have a combined annual impact of more than Rs 10,000 crore on the government exchequer. (ANI)

stories.headline: From JLR to Iveco, Tata Motors’ high-stakes acquisition strategy
stories.title: From JLR to Iveco, Tata Motors’ high-stakes acquisition strategy
stories.summary: Tata Motors has often looked abroad, buying foreign businesses to acquire technology, expand to new markets and accelerate ambitions that would take years to achieve at home. The track record, however, has been mixed.In 2004, it bought South Korea’s Daewoo Commercial Vehicle for about $102 million, gaining a foothold in a market where building a comparable business from scratch could have taken years, if not decades.Four years later, it made a far bolder move, paying about $2.3 billion to buy Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) from Ford Motor.Now, with its €3.9 billion acquisition of Italy’s Iveco Group, Tata Motors is returning to the familiar playbook: Buy a struggling business, leave its brand and management largely intact, and give it time.“Their acquisitions have been driven by the need to have certain technology where developing it internally could end up costing more time,” says Avik Chattopadhyay, founder of the Indian School for Design of Automobiles (INDEA) at XLRI Delhi-NCR. “It’s also about finding newer ways of doing things, of engineering and even designing your product.”Also Read: Tata Motors takes control of Iveco in €3.9 bn deal, eyes global truck marketTrack RecordTata Motors’ international acquisition strategy gathered momentum in the early 2000s, when it acquired Daewoo. The purchase gave the company access to an established South Korean truck manufacturer, its engineering capabilities and a broader product range.The next move was smaller and shows what happens when the market shrinks. Tata acquired a 21 percent stake in Spanish bus and coach manufacturer Hispano Carrocera in 2005, taking full ownership in 2009. It shut the plant four years later, saying the European bus market had suffered its worst-ever decline after the 2008 crisis.Then came JLR, an acquisition that stunned the auto industry. In 2008, when it bought the storied luxury car maker from Ford, Tata had a fledgling passenger vehicle business at home, which, only years ago, it had wanted to sell to Ford. Acquiring the British luxury car brand gave Tata access to globally recognised brands, established distribution networks, engineering centres and manufacturing facilities. It also gave the Indian company an opportunity to participate in a much higher-value segment of the automotive market.The group’s corporate structure has since changed. Tata Motors used to house its passenger and commercial vehicle (CV) businesses together. They were demerged in October 2025 and are now separately listed companies.The passenger vehicle business, which includes JLR, is now Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd. The CV business that is buying Iveco has been branded as Tata Motors.JLR remains the most closely watched acquisition, not just because of the signal it sent about the company’s global ambitions, but also because of its striking initial turnaround.JLR lost £306 million in its first 10 months under Tata. A decade later, in 2017, it posted a pre-tax profit of £1.6 billion. From 2018, the company struggled again, hit by US-China trade tensions, anxiety over Brexit and weak demand for diesel cars in Europe. It has been volatile since, reporting a loss of £244 million after tax in FY26, its first loss since FY23.Also Read: Tata Motors CV turns in profit of Rs1,254 crore; revenue surges 42 percentPlan with IvecoThe Iveco acquisition is different from JLR.JLR gave Tata access to luxury passenger vehicles, globally recognised brands and a higher-margin segment. In CVs, Tata is already a market leader in India with a market share of 36 percent in the first half of FY27. European companies come with a lot of caveats.”Back at Bombay House, Tata Sons Chairman N Chandrasekaran has set an ambitious target of generating $100 billion in auto revenue by FY31. He has pegged the CV business’s contribution at about $40 billion, a goal he outlined at Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles’ annual meeting this year.Chandrasekaran, who is set to join Iveco’s board as chairperson, will have a direct hand in making sure it comes sooner.

In Iveco, Tata gets access to its advanced technologies, including Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) and software-driven vehicles.
Tata also gets multiple powertrains including electric, LNG, hybrid and hydrogen for its CV business in existing markets, according to a Crisil Ratings report from August 2025.
